---
title: "Certified funnels"
subtitle: "Each edge of the contact-formation graph becomes a certified transition: every state of its entry set, for every disk friction in the band, reaches the next edge's entry set. Chained, the edges certify a plan as executed, including motions that use momentum."
---

## The idea

The [hold gate](hold-gate.qmd) and the [box certificate](certificate.qmd)
certify that the box *can be held* at every pose along a plan. A **funnel**
certifies the motion itself:

- **Entry set.** A box of states the edge may start from: pose, velocity,
  contact offsets, and μ<sub>disk</sub> ∈ [0.3, 0.5].
- **Law and tube.** A feedback law and a tube around its nominal motion.
- **Certificate.** For every state in the entry set and every friction in
  the band, the motion stays in the tube, the contact forces stay inside
  their cones and above a derived floor, the motor stays in its box, and the
  edge ends inside the next edge's entry set.
- **Check.** The certified edge is executed in MJX from measured states, and
  the measured coverage is reported at 95/95.

Edges whose sets compose this way form a chain that is certified end to end.
The box no longer has to be held at every instant, so rolls, landings in
motion and coasting become plannable edges.

## Track C: a chain with a landing in motion

The chain tips the box, pivots it on the step corner, breaks and remakes
contact, rolls it over the corner, pushes it so that it lands on the platform
in motion, and transports it to the goal.

| Piece | Certified | MJX from real entry states |
|---|---|---|
| Tip (held departure) | yes | — |
| Pivot to 59.00° (law switch at 23°) | yes | 932 / 932 |
| Stop at 59.00° | yes, with the derived force floor | 768 / 768 |
| Gentle break, then make(m<sub>z</sub>) pressing along the inward normal | yes | 300 / 300 |
| Break(g<sub>v</sub>) delivering the box to the roll | yes | 687 / 687 |
| Roll over the corner | being re-certified from the 62° junction | pending |
| Push and landing in motion | follows the roll | pending |
| Transport to the goal | follows the landing | pending |

The roll is re-searched because the junction at 62° failed: a jump from the
break's 1°/s to the roll's 8°/s violates the sticking cone at the hand-off.
The re-search includes ramped speed profiles. The best certified candidates
so far keep 1°/s through the junction.

## The landing impact is measured, not certified

Every piece above is certified by **interval arithmetic**. Each quantity is
carried as a range guaranteed to contain its true value, the state box is
pushed through the dynamics step by step, and each condition is checked
over the whole box at once.

That fails over the few steps around the landing impact. The reason is the
**wrapping effect**. Intervals store only axis-aligned boxes. Each step
shears and rotates the set, and re-wrapping it in a box adds empty corners
that compound.

A line segment rotated by 45° shows it. The smallest box around the
rotated segment is a square, so the width grows by √2. After 8 such
rotations the box is 16 times wider, while the true set is still a segment.
At impact the velocities flip and couple strongly to where the box hit.
The box grows until nothing can be proved, and splitting it would need
about 10<sup>10</sup> pieces.

The impact window is therefore stated **by measurement**: every MJX landing
ends at rest in the target formation, reported at 95/95.

## A set-based route: zonotopes

The remedy is to certify a **set shape** that a step maps without
re-wrapping. A zonotope is

  **c + G · [−1, 1]<sup>k</sup>**,

a centre plus a linear image of a cube.

- **A linear step maps it exactly.** It just multiplies G. A nonlinear step
  is linearized, its Jacobian multiplies G, and only the small remainder is
  boxed. In validated integration this is Lohner's method, the first-order
  Taylor form.
- **Checks stay cheap.** The minimum of a linear quantity a·x over the
  zonotope is a·c − Σ|a·G|. Force floors and friction cones cost about what
  they cost on boxes.
- **General polytopes don't scale.** Their face and vertex counts grow
  exponentially with the dimension, and a nonlinear map does not map a
  polytope to a polytope.
- **The hard part is the contact switch.** At impact, part of the set is
  already in contact and part is not. The set has to be split along the
  contact guard and each part followed in its own mode. A **hybrid
  zonotope**, a union of constrained zonotopes indexed by binary factors,
  represents exactly such a mode-branched set
  ([Bird, Pangborn, Jain and Koeln, *Automatica* 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14831);
  for nonlinear steps,
  [Siefert et al., ACC 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.09902)).

**First test.** One impact branch and one small entry sub-box, with the
first-order form (a chain-rule Jacobian with an interval remainder)
intersected with the interval box at each step. The decision test was the
size of the entry boxes on which every rocking class after the impact is
excluded. Those boxes grew from 2<sup>−4</sup> to 2<sup>−2</sup> per
coordinate, 2<sup>12</sup> in volume over the window's six coordinates,
against a bar of 2<sup>10</sup> set beforehand.

Step by step the picture is mixed:
- **The make step** encloses the reached set 2<sup>9</sup>–2<sup>13</sup>
  times tighter in volume.
- **The steps before impact** gain almost nothing.
- **The tail step** alone is looser than the interval box, which is why the
  two are intersected.

The other branches and the rest of the landing set are untested.

::: {.callout-note title="If the zonotope route works"}
If zonotopes certify the impact window over the whole landing set, the
landing becomes a certified link, and set-based certificates for
contact-rich funnels deserve to be pursued well beyond this chain.

Justin Koeln and Justin Ruths at UT Dallas work on exactly these set
representations: hybrid zonotopes for reachability of mixed logical
dynamical systems, and the zonoLAB toolbox
([arXiv 2310.15426](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.15426)). That line would be a
natural collaboration.
:::
